name: WCORR-EVAS-001 — sudo → audit configuration change → audit daemon stopped
description: Detects sudo activity followed by an audit configuration change and an audit daemon stop event
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=20m
      [any where rule.id.keyword in ("5402", "5407")]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword == "80705" and
        data.audit.type.keyword == "CONFIG_CHANGE"
      ]
      [any where rule.id.keyword == "80703"]

name: WCORR-MAL-001 — System executable modification → rootcheck anomaly
description: This rule is different from most of the preceding rules because it correlates events using both the Wazuh agent ID and the affected file path. That distinction is important: a rootcheck anomaly on the same endpoint is insufficient unless its data.file.keyword matches the executable path identified by the earlier FIM alert.
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=60m
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in ("550", "554") and
        syscheck.mode.keyword == "realtime" and
        (
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/usr/bin/*" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/usr/sbin/*" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/bin/*" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/sbin/*"
        )
      ] by syscheck.path.keyword
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in ("510", "521") and
        data.file.keyword != null and
        data.file.keyword != "/dev/null\r"
      ] by data.file.keyword

name: WCORR-PERS-001 — SSH login → crontab editor → cron modification
description: Detects an SSH login followed by a crontab editor event and a FIM alert for a cron-related file. The expression requires three chronologically ordered events on the same Wazuh agent, with no more than 30 minutes between the first and final event.
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
      [any where rule.id.keyword == "5715"]
      [any where rule.id.keyword == "2834"]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in ("550", "554") and (
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/var/spool/cron/*" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/var/spool/cron/crontabs/*" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/etc/cron.d/*" or
          syscheck.path.keyword == "/etc/crontab"
        )
      ]

name: WCORR-PERS-002 — SSH login → systemd unit modification → service failure
description: Detects an SSH login followed by modification or creation of a systemd service unit and a subsequent service-failure alert
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
      [any where rule.id.keyword == "5715"]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in ("550", "554") and (
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/etc/systemd/system/*.service" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/usr/lib/systemd/system/*.service" or
          syscheck.path.keyword like "/lib/systemd/system/*.service"
        )
      ]
      [any where rule.id.keyword == "40704"]

name: WCORR-PRIV-001 — SSH access → privileged account creation
description: A successful SSH login, followed by execution of a privileged account-creation command, followed by confirmation that a new Linux user account has been created
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5715"
  ]
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword in ("5402", "5407") and
    data.dstuser.keyword == "root" and
    (
      data.command.keyword like "*useradd*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*adduser*"
    )
  ]
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5902"
  ]

name: WCORR-SSH-001 — Brute-force followed by authentication from the same IP
description: Detects an SSH brute-force alert followed by successful authentication on the same Wazuh agent within 15 minutes
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword, data.srcip.keyword with maxspan=15m
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword in ("5712", "5763") and
    data.srcip.keyword != null
  ]
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5715" and
    data.srcip.keyword != null
  ]

name: WCORR-SSH-002 — SSH followed by sensitive sudo activity
description: The rule detects successful SSH authentication followed by privileged command execution within 15 minutes
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=15m
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5715" and
    data.dstuser.keyword != null
  ]
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword in ("5402", "5407") and
    data.dstuser.keyword == "root" and
    data.command.keyword != null and
    (
      data.command.keyword like "*useradd*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*usermod*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*passwd*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*visudo*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*systemctl disable*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*systemctl stop*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*crontab*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*chmod*" or
      data.command.keyword like "*chown*"
    )
  ]

name: WCORR-SSH-003 — SSH followed by realtime sensitive file modification
description: Correlates remote access with subsequent modification of sensitive Linux authentication or access-control files. This SSH-linked rule is restricted to realtime FIM events
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword == "5715"
  ]
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword in ("550", "554") and
    syscheck.mode.keyword == "realtime" and
    (
      syscheck.path.keyword in (
        "/etc/passwd",
        "/etc/shadow",
        "/etc/group",
        "/etc/gshadow",
        "/etc/sudoers"
      ) or
      syscheck.path.keyword like "/etc/sudoers.d/*" or
      syscheck.path.keyword like "/home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys" or
      syscheck.path.keyword == "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys"
    )
  ]

name: WCORR-SSH-004 — SSH login, sudo and sensitive file modification
description: Detects a three-stage sequence involving remote access, privilege use and modification of security-sensitive files
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
  [any where rule.id.keyword == "5715"]
  [any where rule.id.keyword in ("5402", "5407")]
  [any where
    rule.id.keyword in ("550", "554") and
    (
      syscheck.path.keyword in (
        "/etc/passwd",
        "/etc/shadow",
        "/etc/group",
        "/etc/gshadow",
        "/etc/sudoers"
      ) or
      syscheck.path.keyword like "/etc/sudoers.d/*" or
      syscheck.path.keyword like "/home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys" or
      syscheck.path.keyword == "/root/.ssh/authorized_keys"
    )
  ]

name: WCORR-SSH-005 — SSH login, SCP execution and file modification
description: Detects an SSH login followed by SCP execution and a file creation or modification event
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
      [any where rule.id.keyword == "5715"]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword == "92603" and
        data.audit.command.keyword == "scp"
      ]
      [any where rule.id.keyword in ("550", "554")]

name: WCORR-WEB-001 — Web reconnaissance followed by exploitation attempt
description: This rule correlates reconnaissance and exploitation indicators originating from the same recorded HTTP client IP against the same Wazuh-monitored endpoint
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword, data.srcip.keyword
    with maxspan=10m
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in (
          "31151", "31515", "31516"
        ) and
        data.srcip.keyword != null
      ]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in (
          "31103", "31104", "31105",
          "31110", "31164", "31166", "31168"
        ) and
        data.srcip.keyword != null
      ]

name: WCORR-WEB-002 — Web attack followed by suspicious PHP file creation
description: This rule detects web attack indicators followed by the creation of a PHP file in the WordPress uploads directory
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=10m
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in (
          "31151", "31103", "31104", "31105"
        )
      ]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword == "554" and
        syscheck.event.keyword == "added" and
        syscheck.path.keyword like
          "/var/lib/docker/volumes/web_wp_data/_data/wp-content/uploads/*.php"
      ]

name: WCORR-WEB-003 — Server-side exploitation indicator followed by PHP file creation
description: This rule uses a narrower selection of web exploitation indicators followed by PHP file creation
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=10m
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword in (
          "31106", "31110", "31166", "31168"
        )
      ]
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword == "554" and
        syscheck.event.keyword == "added" and
        syscheck.path.keyword like
          "/var/lib/docker/volumes/web_wp_data/_data/wp-content/uploads/*.php"
      ]

name: WCORR-WEB-004 — PHP file creation followed by HTTP access attempt
description: This is the revised version. Instead of accepting general suspicious web activity after PHP creation, it requires a subsequent HTTP request targeting a PHP URL within the WordPress uploads directory
query:
sequence by agent.id.keyword with maxspan=30m
      [any where
        rule.id.keyword == "554" and
        syscheck.event.keyword == "added" and
        syscheck.path.keyword like
          "/var/lib/docker/volumes/web_wp_data/_data/wp-content/uploads/*.php"
      ]
      [any where
        data.url.keyword != null and
        data.url.keyword like
          "/wp-content/uploads/*.php*"
      ]
